headline: LME copper rebounds more than 3% from an 11-month low
detail: Short covering in thin holiday trade and a weaker dollar lifted copper Thursday; the LME official price rose to $11,965/t from $11,703. Analysts call it a bear-market bounce, with copper still about 20% below its September peak.

headline: Chicago ferrous scrap seen rising about $20 a ton for December
detail: B.L. Duke expects Chicago prime and shredded grades up roughly $20/GT in December after gains in October and November, with US mill utilization up to 81.7% and HRC near $1,355/st. Higher settle would lift yard prices for sheet iron and HMS.

headline: US copper futures jump above $5.50 a pound Friday
detail: COMEX copper is trading near $5.59-5.61/lb early Friday, up over 4% from Wednesday's $5.33 settle, as tech stocks rally; US futures did not settle Thursday for Thanksgiving. Expect yard copper bids to firm if the bounce holds.

headline: North American copper and brass scrap prices tick up
detail: ScrapMonster's index shows copper, brass and bronze scrap edging higher for Nov 26 after a 25-cent copper drop earlier in the week. Bids are following the futures bounce.

headline: Hot core inflation all but locks in a December Fed hike
detail: October core PCE rose to 3.3%, above forecasts and the highest in nearly three years, and futures price about 94-99% odds of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting. Higher rates and a firmer dollar weigh on metals.

headline: Gold rebounds toward $3,650 and silver jumps 6% early Friday
detail: Spot gold climbed about 2.3% to roughly $3,650 early Friday after Thursday's dip to about $3,567, and silver rose to around $44. Gold had touched a 15-month low of $3,446 on Wednesday.

headline: Platinum and palladium climb 3-4% overnight
detail: Kitco quotes late Thursday had platinum near $1,335-1,345 (+3%) and palladium near $894-934 (+4%) after Thursday closes around $1,294 and $861. Better PGM prices help catalytic converter values after a rough month.

headline: Nickel and zinc jump more than 3% as base metals bounce
detail: Three-month nickel rose about 3.7% to $15,731/t and zinc about 3.3% Thursday, with lead and tin also higher. The LME official nickel price rose to $15,665/t from $15,035.

headline: Steel lead times stretch past 10 weeks for hot-rolled
detail: Average mill lead times now reach into mid-February and plate set another record, the longest waits for most sheet since 2021. Tight mills support strong scrap demand into December.

headline: LME aluminum squeeze eases after lending rule change
detail: The LME cut the lending-rule trigger to 30% of available stocks from 50% and halved the wait for new smelter brands to six months, narrowing front-month spreads. Cash aluminum had fallen 8.7% on Wednesday as the squeeze broke.

headline: Nucor lifts its hot-rolled coil price to $1,330 a ton
detail: Nucor raised its weekly consumer spot price $20 to $1,330/st, extending a long run of increases. Strong steel prices keep mills hungry for scrap.

headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies over overproduction
detail: USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs of up to about 15-20% on China, the EU, Taiwan and others; comments are due Jan 5 and no start date is set. Broader trade fights add uncertainty for metal demand.

headline: US signals it may ease steel, aluminum and auto tariffs for Canada
detail: Trade chief Jamieson Greer said the US wants a deal that accommodates Canada on steel, aluminum and autos, which now face 25% Section 232 duties set to double in January. A deal would change cross-border metal flows into the Midwest.

headline: China's industrial profits jump 20% in October
detail: Profits at Chinese industrial firms rose 20.1% year on year in October, the fastest in five months, led by electronics. Better factory earnings support metal demand, though property remains weak.

headline: Chinese copper scrap dealers pull back as prices swing
detail: Shanghai copper fell about 3,600 yuan/t this week and secondary scrap quotes were cut about 6,000 yuan/t, so many suppliers held back material. Thin Chinese scrap flows can support copper cathode demand.

headline: China aluminum stocks fall to a five-year seasonal low
detail: Chinese aluminum ingot inventories fell 18,000 t on the week, the lowest for this time of year in five years, while LME three-month aluminum closed near $2,808 Thursday. Low stocks limit downside after this week's slide.

headline: Stellantis plans more European plant shutdowns
detail: Stellantis will pause plants in Mulhouse and Rennes for parts of December and January and cut about 500 temporary jobs at Sochaux, citing weak demand and Chinese competition. Fewer cars built means less steel, aluminum and PGM demand.

headline: Cox sees November US auto sales at a 15.8 million pace
detail: Cox forecasts about 1.2 million new vehicles sold in November, down 7% from a year ago on fewer selling days, but the annual pace improves to 15.8 million from 15.5 million. Steady sales keep auto scrap and PGM demand stable.

headline: Rhodium holds near $8,650 while dealer quotes stay wide
detail: Kitco's rhodium bid/ask midpoint was unchanged at $8,650 Thursday, while Umicore's price eased to $8,800 on Nov 25 from $8,950 a week earlier. Softer rhodium trims catalytic converter values.

headline: Gold slipped Thursday as Fed hike bets held
detail: In thin holiday trade, spot gold dipped about 0.6% to near $3,566 Thursday while silver edged up, with markets pricing a December rate hike and a firm dollar.

headline: Scrap expected to keep rising after lagging the steel rally
detail: Steel Market Update notes hot-rolled coil climbed sharply this year while busheling lagged, and scrap is now expected to firm on seasonal factors and tight supply. That points to a steady-to-higher December settle for prime and obsolete grades.

headline: US copper premium turns to a discount and stockpiled metal heads back to China
detail: With LME copper about 20% below its September peak, the US price is now below London, so tariff-driven US stocks are being shipped out, mostly to China, where import premiums hit a record. That is bearish for domestic copper scrap spreads.

headline: Vanke seeks a three-year delay on a bond payment as property stress deepens
detail: The developer wants to push back a 1.2 billion yuan payment due Dec 15, with its sales down nearly half. More property distress means less construction steel demand in the biggest metals market.

headline: October new home sales jump 14% to the best pace of 2026
detail: Sales rose to a 701,000 annual pace as builders cut prices, though the Midwest is still down for the year. A modest lift for rebar, wire and HVAC copper demand.

headline: Fed Beige Book says construction weakened while manufacturing grew modestly
detail: Most districts saw slight growth, but residential real estate and construction softened on high borrowing costs, and contacts named metals and tariffs as cost pressures. Mixed signal for steel and scrap demand.

headline: Dollar holds near 103.75 as Treasury yields slip to a 3-month low
detail: The dollar is off its recent 20-month high while the 10-year yield fell to about 4.80% on haven buying. A strong dollar still keeps pressure on dollar-priced metals.

headline: First Quantum accepts Panama's terms for talks on Cobre Panama
detail: Formal talks on the mine, shut since 2023 and once about 1% of world copper supply, began Nov 23. A restart is still far off but raises the prospect of more copper later.

headline: Chinese zinc smelters restart after maintenance
detail: Smelters in several provinces came back online, adding refined supply and pushing zinc lower even as mine supply stays tight. Adds pressure on zinc and die-cast scrap values.

headline: Iron ore stays near a four-year low
detail: Chinese iron ore futures hit a four-year low in mid-November and 62% Fe sat near $89-91/t on weak steel output and high port stocks. Cheap ore helps blast furnaces compete with scrap-fed mills overseas.

headline: US scrap export market stays quiet as Turkish buying slows
detail: The last confirmed US cargo to Turkey was in late October near $398.50/t CFR for HMS 80:20, and Turkish mills have since bought sparingly from Europe. Weak export demand removes a prop for obsolete grades.
